subject: Recap & next steps: target $/1M token benchmarking (Redwood vs OpenAI/Anthropic/hosts)
messages:
From: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa@redwood.com>
To: Alex Johnson <alex.j@acme.com>, Olivia Smith <olivia.smith@acme.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 4 Mar 2027 15:10:00 -0700
Subject: Recap & next steps: token economics & target $/1M benchmark

Hi Alex + Olivia —

Thanks again for the time today. Quick recap and the concrete next steps we discussed on target pricing per 1M tokens. Trying to distill the call into a concise mutual action plan so everyone is aligned.

Summary / what we heard from you:
- Short-term POC volume: ~50-100M tokens/mo.
- Long-term ramp target: 1B-5B tokens/mo (user-facing generation + reranking flows).
- Primary SLA/latency requirement: 200-400ms p95 for user queries.
- Budget guidance: target monthly spend ~ $20k-$200k depending on scale; you called out a target unit price of roughly $25 / 1M tokens to make the economics work.

Redwood benchmarking (high-level):
- Redwood (open-model hosts on our Dedicated pools, 8-bit quantized): ~$15-$30 per 1M tokens depending on model family, batching, and KV-cache savings.
- OpenAI (GPT-4-style commercial endpoints): significantly higher for GPT-4-class models (order of magnitude higher for comparable capability) - typical ~$150-$300 per 1M tokens depending on prompt length and model.
- Anthropic (Claude-class): mid-range vs GPT-4; ballpark ~$80-$150 per 1M tokens for higher-capability models.
- Other open-model hosts/self-hosted options: widely variable - $25-$60 per 1M tokens depending on hosting, orchestration overhead, and model efficiency.

Important caveats / levers that materially change $/1M:
- Model selection (open weights vs hosted commercial grade) - capability-to-cost tradeoff.
- Quantization: 8-bit/4-bit gives big savings vs float32 but may affect quality; we can recommend profiles based on your evals.
- Caching & prefix reuse: we typically see 20-40% token savings on chat-style apps from prefix/KV cache.
- Batching & concurrency: improves unit cost but can add small latency tradeoffs; Redwood Optimize suggests per-route configs automatically.

Concrete deliverables we agreed to share:
1) Spreadsheet with a modeled example for your two volume scenarios (50-100M POC and 1-5B scale) - includes per-1M breakdowns, expected monthly spend, and sensitivity to caching/quantization. (attached: acme-1M-token-benchmarking.xlsx)
2) Redwood pricing summary + recommended config for hitting your $25 / 1M target at scale (attached: redwood-pricing-summary.pdf).
3) Quick follow-up call to walk the modeled numbers and discuss any performance/quality tradeoffs - suggested times below.

Next steps / ask from Acme:
- Confirm which models you want modeled in the sheet (recommended: Mistral-like open model + a smaller cost-optimized Llama variant).
- Share any sample prompts or average prompt/response lengths (tokens in/out) so we can make the modeled example more accurate.

Available for a follow-up: tomorrow 9:30-11:00am PT or Friday 10-2pm PT. If those don't work, propose two times and we'll lock it.

Thanks - happy to iterate on the spreadsheet after you review.

- Vanessa Ortiz
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
vanessa@redwood.com | +1 415-555-0194

Attachments: acme-1M-token-benchmarking.xlsx (spreadsheet), redwood-pricing-summary.pdf (one-pager)
From: Alex Johnson <alex.j@acme.com>
To: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Cc: Olivia Smith <olivia.smith@acme.com>
Date: Thu, 4 Mar 2027 17:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Recap & next steps: token economics & target $/1M benchmark

Vanessa - thanks for the clear notes and attachments. A couple quick clarifications before we dig into the spreadsheet:

1) When you quote Redwood $15-$30 / 1M tokens, is that assuming dedicated Reserved capacity (we pay for reserved GPUs) or hosted burstable capacity? We're trying to model an enterprise committed price.
2) Our target $25 / 1M is for production user-facing queries (inference only). We expect 30% of requests to be similar prefixes (i.e., cacheable). Please model both the raw and effective (post-cache) $/1M.
3) Curious how you accounted for request/response token counts - e.g., are you modeling 300 tokens in + 700 tokens out per request (total 1k tokens)? We'll attach a couple sample prompts, but if you can model `avg_in=300 / avg_out=700` that'll be close.

Also - if you can include a side-by-side monthly spend comparison vs OpenAI/Anthropic for the POC and scale scenarios (same token counts), that would be very helpful for procurement.

Available for the follow-up Fri 11am PT if that works.

- Alex
Director, Product Platform | Acme Corp
alex.j@acme.com
From: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa@redwood.com>
To: Alex Johnson <alex.j@acme.com>, Olivia Smith <olivia.smith@acme.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 4 Mar 2027 18:22:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Recap & next steps: token economics & target $/1M benchmark

Thanks Alex - great details. Quick answers and I've updated the attached spreadsheet with the scenarios you asked for (see tab names: POC_50-100M and Scale_1B-5B).

Short answers:
- Redwood $ range assumes Dedicated reserved capacity (committed monthly) with standard autoscale headroom. We show both committed-only and committed+burst columns in the sheet.
- Caching: we model 30% prefix reuse for your flows (so effective tokens billed = 70% of raw), and included a sensitivity +/-10%.
- Token assumptions: I modeled avg_in=300 / avg_out=700 as you suggested (1k total tokens per request).

Sample modeled outputs (from the spreadsheet, high-level):
- POC (50M raw tokens/mo; 30% caching => 35M billed):
  - Redwood committed (quantized, dedicated): ~$630-$1,050 / mo => corresponds to ~$18-$30 per 1M billed tokens (varies by model).
  - OpenAI (GPT-4 equivalent): ~$5,250-$10,500 / mo (rough ballpark).
  - Anthropic (Claude-equivalent): ~$2,800-$5,250 / mo (rough ballpark).

- Scale (1B raw tokens/mo; 30% caching => 700M billed):
  - Redwood committed (recommended config): ~$12,600-$21,000 / mo => ~$18-$30 per 1M billed tokens.
  - OpenAI: materially higher - ~$175k-$350k / mo (depending on model).
  - Anthropic: ~$90k-$150k / mo.

Notes: the large absolute gaps are driven by model-class pricing differences. For many enterprise use-cases, the open-model route on Redwood Dedicated lets you hit target unit economics while retaining fine-grained control over model selection, quant, and routing policies.

Attached updated spreadsheet and a one-pager pricing summary. I also included a tab with the per-request sample calc so your procurement team can see the math line-by-line.

I'll be on the call Fri 11am PT - I've tentatively booked it on my side. If you want Marissa (pricing lead) to join, I can loop her in.

- Vanessa
